sections.purpose: To define the requirements, selection, donning, doffing, disposal, and maintenance of Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) in pharmacy laboratories to minimize occupational exposure to chemical, biological, and physical hazards.
sections.scope: Applicable to all students, faculty, laboratory staff, researchers, and visitors in all laboratories of the institution.
procedure: Select appropriate PPE based on the specific hazards of the laboratory and experiment being conducted, as detailed in the Safety Data Sheet (SDS) and lab safety guidelines.
Inspect all PPE items for damage, wear, or defects prior to donning. Do not use compromised PPE.

Donning sequence: (1) Perform hand hygiene; (2) Put on laboratory coat/gown and button it completely; (3) Put on safety goggles/face shield; (4) Put on appropriate gloves, ensuring the cuffs extend over the lab coat sleeves.
Ensure lab coats are long-sleeved, knee-length, and remain fully buttoned at all times while in the laboratory.
Choose gloves compatible with the chemicals being handled (e.g., nitrile for general chemistry, latex for biology, neoprene/butyl for strong solvents/acids, heat-resistant for autoclaves/furnaces).
Wear safety goggles with side shields that meet safety standards (e.g., ANSI Z87.1) for all activities involving chemicals, heat, or glassware under pressure/vacuum.
Use respiratory protection (N95 or chemical cartridge respirators) when handling volatile, toxic powders or working in environments with airborne particulate hazards.
Avoid touching personal items (phones, laptops, keys) or door handles with contaminated gloves.

Doffing sequence: (1) Remove gloves using the glove-to-glove and skin-to-skin technique to prevent self-contamination; (2) Perform hand hygiene; (3) Remove safety goggles/face shield; (4) Remove lab coat; (5) Perform hand hygiene again.
Dispose of single-use PPE (gloves, masks) in designated biohazard or chemical waste containers. Never mix with regular office trash.
Wash reusable PPE (lab coats, safety goggles, face shields) regularly. Store them in clean, designated lockers or cabinets outside the main working lab space.
Report any skin contact or exposure resulting from PPE failure immediately to the Laboratory In-charge.
precautions: PPE is the last line of defense; it does not eliminate hazards but only provides a barrier.
Never wear open-toed shoes, sandals, or high heels in the laboratory. Shoes must be fully closed and slip-resistant.
Tie back long hair and secure loose clothing or jewelry before entering the laboratory.
Do not wear contact lenses in chemical laboratories unless splash goggles are worn constantly.
Never wear laboratory coats, gloves, or other protective gear in non-laboratory areas (e.g., cafeterias, libraries, offices, restrooms).
Change gloves immediately if they become torn, punctured, or contaminated with a chemical splash.
Wash hands thoroughly with soap and water after removing gloves and before leaving the laboratory.
